---
title: "Bar charts"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8.8, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 100,
  fig.retina = 2, dev = "ragg_png", out.width = "100%"
)
options(gglaplot2.font = "inter")
library(ggplot2)
library(gglaplot2)
gbp <- scales::label_dollar(prefix = "£", scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k")
a <- gla_yearly[gla_yearly$series == "Variable A", ]
```

Bars are `data-primary` with a 1px `chart-surface` edge, so stacked segments
and neighbouring bars keep a hairline between them, and they fill a little
over half the slot. The value axis starts at zero and the baseline is drawn.

## Single variable

```{r single}
ggplot(a, aes(factor(year), average)) +
  geom_gla_col() +
  gla_zero_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), labels = gbp, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  gla_labs(
    title = "Variable A's yearly average has halved since 2016",
    subtitle = "London yearly average variable value (GBP), 2015 to 2024",
    source = "LDN Viz Tools demo data", byline = "GLA City Intelligence", x = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gla()
```

## Stacked

```{r stacked}
ggplot(gla_yearly, aes(factor(year), average, fill = series)) +
  geom_gla_col() +
  gla_zero_line() +
  scale_fill_gla() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), labels = gbp, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  gla_labs(
    title = "The three variables together", subtitle = "Yearly average value (GBP)",
    source = "LDN Viz Tools demo data", x = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gla()
```

## Grouped

`position = "dodge"` lays the bars out the way the web charts' grouped bar
charts do: each category's bars side by side in a slot of their own, close
together, with a clear gap before the next category, in the series order
the fill scale gives them. The legend stays, as it does on the web; a
grouped chart has too many bars to label each.

```{r grouped}
recent <- gla_yearly[gla_yearly$year >= 2020, ]
ggplot(recent, aes(factor(year), average, fill = series)) +
  geom_gla_col(position = "dodge") +
  gla_zero_line() +
  scale_fill_gla() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), labels = gbp, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  gla_labs(
    title = "Variable A has fallen furthest", subtitle = "Yearly average value (GBP), 2020 to 2024",
    source = "LDN Viz Tools demo data", x = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gla()
```

The spacing is `position_gla_dodge()`, which can be given directly to change
it. A category with a bar missing keeps the others at the same width rather
than stretching them to fill the slot.

## Horizontal grouped

The same with the category on `y`. The web version puts each category's
label on the left with its bars beside it; here the category is the y axis.

```{r horizontal-grouped, fig.height = 4.4}
ggplot(recent, aes(average, factor(year), fill = series)) +
  geom_gla_col(position = "dodge") +
  gla_zero_line("x") +
  scale_fill_gla() +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), labels = gbp, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  gla_labs(
    title = "Variable A has fallen furthest", subtitle = "Yearly average value (GBP), 2020 to 2024",
    source = "LDN Viz Tools demo data", x = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gla(gridlines = "x")
```

## Faceted

```{r faceted, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(gla_yearly, aes(factor(year), average, fill = series)) +
  geom_gla_col() +
  gla_zero_line() +
  facet_wrap(vars(series), ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_gla() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), labels = gbp, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  gla_labs(title = "Each variable on its own", subtitle = "Yearly average value (GBP)", x = NULL) +
  theme_gla(legend = "none")
```

## Horizontal

Map the category to `y`, put the gridlines on `x`, and the baseline on the
left. Order the bars by value unless the categories have an order of their
own.

```{r horizontal, fig.height = 3}
y24 <- gla_yearly[gla_yearly$year == 2024, ]
ggplot(y24, aes(average, reorder(series, average))) +
  geom_gla_col() +
  gla_zero_line("x") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), labels = gbp, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  gla_labs(title = "Variable A was the largest in 2024", subtitle = "Average value (GBP), 2024",
           source = "LDN Viz Tools demo data", x = NULL) +
  theme_gla(gridlines = "x")
```

## Horizontal stacked

```{r horizontal-stacked, fig.height = 3}
two <- gla_yearly[gla_yearly$year %in% c(2015, 2021), ]
ggplot(two, aes(average, factor(year), fill = series)) +
  geom_gla_col() +
  gla_zero_line("x") +
  scale_fill_gla() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), labels = gbp, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  gla_labs(title = "2015 against 2021", subtitle = "Average value (GBP)", x = NULL) +
  theme_gla(gridlines = "x")
```
